summary:
Alberta is a province of Canada and stands under the national framework. Alberta's own human rights statute prohibits discrimination on the basis of gender identity and gender expression in employment, housing and in public and private accommodation, giving a visitor or resident a provincial route to complain against a landlord, employer or service provider.

Alberta's statutory package for trans people is aimed at minors, school instruction and organised sport. The Education Amendment Act 2024 cleared the final legislative stage on 4 December 2024, introducing parental opt-in for classroom instruction together with rules on student pronouns and sport; a companion health-statutes act bars certain gender-affirming care for minors; the Fairness and Safety in Sport Act sets sports policy. Egale Canada and the Skipping Stone Foundation announced constitutional litigation against the package, calling it discriminatory.

Bill 9, the Protecting Alberta's Children Statutes Amendment Act, 2025, passed at the close of the fall sitting and invokes the Charter's notwithstanding clause to shield the three laws from legal challenge for years. Egale Canada, the Skipping Stone Foundation and five families have said their court challenge to the 2024 health-statutes act continues regardless. The laws are in force while that litigation is pending.

The package's announced scope stops short of detention and shared facilities. Premier Danielle Smith's 12 February 2024 announcement stated the bans would not include women's shelters, women's prisons or women's changing rooms, and no provincial rule placing trans prisoners by birth sex has been enacted. No Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement, special unit or segregation case is documented. Provincial correctional policies vary, and no Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement rule is on the record, so a trans visitor held in provincial custody in Alberta is not subject to any documented trans-specific placement standard.

Legal gender recognition in Alberta runs through vital statistics: birth certificates fall under provincial jurisdiction, and trans people can change their legal gender in every province under rules that vary between them.
tangentialFactors:
The Alberta measures were announced on 12 February 2024 and enacted by 4 December 2024, with the notwithstanding shield added only after the advocacy groups had announced their constitutional challenge. The sequence indicates the legislature applied the override in anticipation of Charter litigation, so the pending case will not suspend the laws while the declaration stands.

Alberta's own statutory history shows Charter equality litigation has previously succeeded against the province: in Vriend v Alberta (1998) the Supreme Court held that the omission of sexual orientation from Alberta's human rights legislation itself violated section 15. That route is foreclosed for the 2024 package by the notwithstanding declaration, which is the substantive difference between the two episodes.

The exposure created by the package is concentrated on minors, parents and school communities. Adult trans visitors fall largely outside its operation: the care ban addresses minors, the instruction and pronoun rules address school settings, and the sport rules address organised competition, while shelters, prisons and changing rooms were expressly left out of the announced scope.
localsOnly:
The Education Amendment Act 2024 requires parental opt-in for classroom instruction and sets rules governing student pronouns and participation in sport. The companion health-statutes act bars certain gender-affirming medical care for minors, and the Fairness and Safety in Sport Act governs trans participation in sport, including the exclusion of trans women from women's competition announced in February 2024.

Residents facing discrimination on the basis of gender identity or gender expression in employment, housing or accommodation may proceed under Alberta's human rights statute, which lists both grounds as prohibited.

Changing the gender marker on an Alberta birth certificate is a provincial vital-statistics matter, as in every province, under rules that vary by jurisdiction.

The 2024 measures are subject to continuing constitutional litigation brought by Egale Canada, the Skipping Stone Foundation and five families, while remaining in force under the notwithstanding declaration.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the pending constitutional challenge will be heard, and on what timetable, while the notwithstanding declaration stands is unresolved; no ruling is sourced.

No Alberta-specific data on hate crime against trans people is sourced, and no Alberta breakdown of reported incidents by gender identity is available in the material reviewed.

No Alberta-specific trans-prisoner placement rule, incident or litigation case is documented. Provincial correctional policy on placement of trans detainees is described as varying without an Alberta rule being identified.

The procedural requirement Alberta imposes for a gender-marker change on a birth certificate — declaration, court order or medical evidence — is not sourced.

Whether the announced exclusion of women's shelters, women's prisons and women's changing rooms from the package will hold in regulation and in practice is not sourced.

No Alberta-specific polling on social acceptance of trans people is sourced.
